Q: How can I select a single field for all documents in a MongoDB collection? A:

Here you go, three ways of doing it. The shortest to boring:

db.student.find({}, 'roll _id'); // <--- Just multiple fields name space separated

// Or
db.student.find({}).select('roll _id'); // <--- Just multiple fields name space separated

// Or
db.student.find({}, {'roll' : 1 , '_id' : 1 ); // <---- Old lengthy boring way

To remove a specific field, use the - operator:

db.student.find({}).select('roll -_id') // <--- Will remove id from the result

Q: How to make a SQL query on a field which can be NULL and values, and only chose the largest value if possible A:

You haven't tagged your request with a particular DBMS, so you want a standard SQL answer.

In standard SQL this is straight-forward and very simple at that: Rank the rows ordered by the value, largest first, nulls being considered last. Then keep the rows with the rank #1.

SELECT *
FROM tb
ORDER BY RANK() OVER (ORDER BY fd DESC NULLS LAST)
FETCH FIRST ROW WITH TIES;

If you are not familiar with FETCH WITH TIES, you might prefer the explicit comparison with #1:

SELECT *
FROM
(
  SELECT tb.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY fd DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk
  FROM tb
) ranked
WHERE rnk = 1;

Q: Problem with sorting months in mysql database A:

You can use the numeric month for correct ordering, and returns the most popular lens per month (across all years). Something like this:

WITH a AS (
    SELECT 
        MONTH(`date`) AS month_num,
        DATE_FORMAT(`date`, '%M') AS month_name,
        lens,
        COUNT(*) AS N
    FROM tb_exifinfo
    GROUP BY month_num, month_name, lens
),
b AS (
    SELECT 
        month_num,
        MAX(N) AS maxN
    FROM a
    GROUP BY month_num
)
SELECT 
    a.month_name AS month,
    a.lens,
    a.N
FROM a
JOIN b 
  ON a.month_num = b.month_num 
 AND a.N = b.maxN
ORDER BY a.month_num;

Q: Getting started with keycloak and kubernetes A:

I've had success with the following Helm chart:

  • https://github.com/codecentric/helm-charts

I created a values.yaml file e.g.

command:
  - "/opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh"
  - "start"
  - "--http-port=8080"
  - "--hostname-strict=false"
extraEnv: |
  - name: KEYCLOAK_ADMIN
    value: admin
  - name: KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD
    value: admin
  - name: JAVA_OPTS_APPEND
    value: >-
      -Djgroups.dns.query={{ include "keycloak.fullname" . }}-headless

service:
  type: NodePort

This is based on https://github.com/codecentric/helm-charts/tree/master/charts/keycloakx with the addition of the service.type: NodePort (so the admin can be accessed on http://localhost:<node-port> URL).

NOTE: You can remove service.type: NodePort which will require e.g. port-forwarding to access KeyCloak.

Once values.yaml file is created then run:

# Add the repo as follows
helm repo add codecentric https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts

# Create namespace
kubectl create namespace keycloak

# Install Keycloak
helm install keycloak codecentric/keycloakx -n keycloak --values ./values.yaml

This will install KeyCloak, to see running port run:

kubectl -n keycloak get service

Returns something like:

NAME                          TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)                                      AGE
keycloak-keycloakx-headless   ClusterIP   None            <none>        80/TCP                                       49m
keycloak-keycloakx-http       NodePort    10.103.232.89   <none>        9000:31800/TCP,80:31366/TCP,8443:30584/TCP   49m

You can see the laptop node port i.e. 31366 so the Keycloak UI can be accessed via:

  • http://localhost:31366

Q: How can I loop through a JSON file using bash and extract values to variables? A:

Use jq only once!!

Try this:

while IFS=, read -r envName val1 val2; do
    echo "for $envName the first value is $val1 and the second value is $val2"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | to_entries[] | .key + "," + ( .value | join(",") )' < vars.json
)

for environment1 the first value is Value1 and the second value is Value2
for environment2 the first value is Value3 and the second value is Value4

or this:

while IFS=, read -ra row; do
    envName="${row[0]}" vals=("${row[@]:1}")
    echo "for $envName values are: [ ${vals[*]@Q} ]"
done < <(                                                                           
   jq -r '.[] | to_entries[] | .key + "," + ( .value | join(",") )' < vars.json
)

for environment1 values are: [ 'Value1' 'Value2' ]
for environment2 values are: [ 'Value3' 'Value4' ]

But if you really wanna do bash loops

while read -r envName; do
    { read -r val1;
      read -r val2 ; } < <(
          jq -r ".[].$envName|.[]" vars.json
    )
    echo "for $envName the first value is $val1 and the second value is $val2"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | keys | .[]' <vars.json
)

for environment1 the first value is Value1 and the second value is Value2
for environment2 the first value is Value3 and the second value is Value4

or

while read -r envName; do
    mapfile -t vals < <(
        jq -r ".[].$envName | .[]" vars.json
    )
    echo "for $envName, values are: [ ${vals[*]@Q} ]"
done < <(
    jq -r '.[] | keys | .[]' <vars.json
)

for environment1, values are: [ 'Value1' 'Value2' ]
for environment2, values are: [ 'Value3' 'Value4' ]
